doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Barry Manilow Johnny Mercer album
summary: She recalls being asked on an elevator in Osaka and singing When October Goes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Then there was a very unusual album with Barry Manilow.
It was very big. It was very unusual . . .
That’s right. What do you remember about that album?
That there was Mercer lyrics – Johnny Mercer lyrics. Barry is delightful, fun to work with, easy. I was asked to do this album in an elevator in Osaka.

Ran into the producer on an elevator, and he told me that Manilow was getting ready to have this thing he wanted to do and would I be interested in doing a Mercer album with Barry Manilow? Who’s going to say no? Barry’s delightful to work with. This was easy, a piece of cake. Here again, you get to know the material.
When October Goes. Oh, wonderful, wonderful material.
That’s one of the ones I heard you pull out of the air at an audience request, after not doing it for many, many years.
I did it not too long ago.
I hadn’t done it in forever – in years.
